slides.heading: Equal vs Assignment
slides.body: Equal vs Assignment is part of Boolean Logic and Comparisons. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Equal vs Assignment
slides.body: The single equals sign = assigns a value. The double equals sign == compares two values for equality.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Assignment is putting a label on a box, while equality comparison checks whether two labels match.

annotations.note: This line stores or updates a value using a variable.
This line displays a value or message on the screen.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Boolean expressions must produce True or False. Use comparisons and logical operators carefully.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Assign password to "open", then check if it equals "open".

quiz.prompt_text: What is the difference between = and == in Python?

options: = assigns a value to a variable and == compares two values

quiz.explanation: Spot on! = assigns a value like score = 10, while == compares two values and returns True or False. Using the wrong one is a common beginner mistake.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines to assign a score and then check if it equals 10.
quiz.explanation: The comment is first, then = assigns the value 10, and finally == compares score to 10 inside print() which outputs True.

quiz.prompt_text: Assign the string open to a variable named password, then print whether it equals open.
quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: print(password == "open") outputs True because the stored value matches. Remember: = stores, == checks.
